# Cold-Weather Construction Equipment Selection for a Mongolian Mining Operation: Caterpillar vs. Komatsu vs. Volvo CE, with Russian-Made Alternatives

## Executive Summary

For a -40°C mining operation in Mongolia, the evidence supports a primary fleet of **Komatsu and Caterpillar** equipment, with **BelAZ** as a cost-effective Russian/CIS supplement. **Volvo CE should be excluded** for primary fleet duty because it has no verified dedicated construction-equipment dealer in Mongolia; parts must be air-freighted from Mumbai in 5–7 days, which is unacceptable for production mining at extreme cold [https://partstrading.com/suppliers/volvo-parts-mongolia/]. The single most decisive factor across all three Western OEMs is that **no machine starts unaided at -40°C** — every fleet requires factory cold-weather packages, 400V shore power infrastructure, and arctic-grade diesel (GOST R 55475-2013, CFPP ≤ -44°C) [https://meganorms.com/gost-r-55475-2013.html].

---

## 1. Cold-Weather Operation at -40°C

### 1.1 Caterpillar

Caterpillar's standard production cold-start capability for large hydraulic mining equipment is -18°C (0°F), with optional "Cold Weather Packages" that add engine coolant heaters, engine oil heaters, hydraulic oil heaters, cab pre-heaters, fuel preheaters/blenders, hydraulic oil cooler bypass valves, and require external 400V/208V three-phase power (~50 kW) [https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20210601-35dac-75766; https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20240220-31ab5-16ec1]. With the cold-start block heater option on the Cat 395 excavator, machine cold-start capability extends to -32°C (-25°F) [https://www.cat.com/en_US/products/new/equipment/excavators/large-excavators/126440.html].

The Cat 793/797F supports **antifreeze/coolant rated to -50°C (-58°F)** as standard extended-life coolant, with engine delay shutdown timer and Mesabi flexible-core radiator [https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20220718-d7a55-ddf05]. The Cat 824 Wheel Dozer supports antifreeze rated to -50°C [https://www.fabickcat.com/new-equipment/824-wheel-dozer/]. The Cat 793 cab heater is rated 36,510 BTU/hr (10.7 kW) with ambient capability to -30°C; at -40°C the standard cab heater reaches its limit and operators should spec the Deluxe Cold Weather Cab [https://www.kellytractor.com/eng/images/pdf/earthmoving/offhighway_trucks/797F.pdf]. Modular field assembly of the Cat 6020B hydraulic mining shovel was validated at -30°C at the same 14-day average assemble time as temperate conditions [https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20160201-48357-52819].

### 1.2 Komatsu

Komatsu Mining Germany (KMG) explicitly rates its hydraulic shovels for ambient temperatures **down to -50°C** when equipped with preheating for diesel engine, water, hydraulic oil, and lubrication systems. Below -25°C, ordinary operation must halt and external electrical preheating engaged; hydraulic oil temperature must reach -20°C (viscosity ~1000 cSt) before the main drive engine can be started [https://onemine.org/documents/adaptation-of-hydraulic-shovels-for-arctic-temperature-of-yakutia-region].

The Komatsu PC4000-6 (400 t class) has a full pre-heating system: KIM HOTSTART engine coolant heating with thermostat, engine oil reserve tank with heater element, and an engine-independent HYDRONIC auxiliary cab heater with programmable start times that keeps the cab warm during standstill periods [https://www.manualslib.com/manual/3641219/Komatsu-Pc4000-6.html?page=151; https://www.manualslib.com/manual/3641219/Komatsu-Pc4000-6.html?page=95]. Komatsu also produces factory "EXTREME COLD TERRAIN SPEC" variants, e.g., the PC400-7 (JPN) with its own field assembly manual [https://manuals-komatsu.com/shop/komatsu-pdf-download-1/pc400-7jpn-extreme-cold-terrain-spec-s-n-50001-up-field-assembly-manual-english/].

For haul trucks, the Komatsu 930E-5, 980E-5, and 860E-1K all support cold-weather packages: electric heaters for coolant, engine oil, hydraulic oil (220V), double-wall exhaust tubes, radiator shutters, cold-weather suspensions, and (for 980E-5) heated exhaust-body routing to prevent payload freeze-sticking [https://www.komatsu.com/en-us/products/equipment/trucks/electric-drive-mining-trucks/980e-5; https://www.komatsu.com/en-us/products/equipment/trucks/electric-drive-mining-trucks/860e-1k; https://www.komatsu.jp/en/-/media/home/aboutus/innovation/technology/techreport/2017/en/180330_06e.pdf].

**Critical field validation:** Oyu Tolgoi has operated **28 Komatsu 930E-4SE trucks** in the South Gobi since **August 2012**, where winter temperatures routinely reach -40°C [https://en.eot.mn/open-pit-mine]. Erdenet Mining Corporation accumulated ~16,000 operating hours on Komatsu HD1500-8 trucks over two years (from a December 2024 delivery of 10 units) and reported that haulage volume increased **7.9%** and cost per m³ of rock haulage decreased **5.8%** after introduction [https://www.linkedin.com/posts/transwest-mongolia_komatsu-komatsuhd1500-hd1500-activity-7500022394456092672-Wf2J; https://erdenettoday.mn/art/7169].

Empirical evidence from a study of Komatsu D-375A/A5 dozers in northern Russia indicates failure flow rises from 2× to 6× at low temperatures relative to warm-season operations, with -25°C identified as a critical threshold for rubber/polymer part embrittlement [https://exa.ai/library/publication/9vvm1yl0lv4]. Komatsu equipment technically operates at -40°C but reliability degrades materially without active arctic packages.

### 1.3 Volvo CE

Volvo CE's articulated haulers (A25–A60 series) and large crawler excavators (e.g., EC950E) carry no OEM-published -40°C cold-start rating in the materials reviewed; their articulated hauling concept is marketed for year-round adverse-weather utilization rather than extreme-cold certification [https://www.volvoce.com/united-states/en-us/products/articulated-haulers/a60/]. The Volvo EC950E lists only an air intake heater and cyclone pre-cleaner — no -40°C arctic package was found in any reviewed Volvo CE document [https://www.volvoce.com/-/media/aprimo/pdf/crawler-excavators/ec950e/brochure-ec950e-t2-en-30-20050247-e.pdf]. Volvo's own cold-weather prep guide warns of "hard starts, higher fuel consumption, less power output" and advises against overnight idling below 1,100 rpm due to cylinder-wall fuel washing [https://www.volvoce.com/en-us/discover/guides-and-advice/2021/diesel-engine-dos-and-donts-to-prep-for-winter-season/].

The only Volvo rigid hauler evidence in Mongolia is a trading-office listing for the R100E (95 t) [https://www.engineering10.com/MN/Ulaanbaatar/104317184885421/Volvo-Mongolia] — a class below the Cat 785/789 and Komatsu 930E, with no arctic package or service network documented.

### 1.4 Liebherr (European alternative for excavator alignment)

For pairing with BelAZ or Komatsu trucks, Liebherr's R 9150 G7 (150 t, ~565 kW) is designed for extreme temperatures, with the "Arctic Package" developed for ALROSA's Udachny mine operating **-55°C to +40°C** with on-site 24/7 Liebherr service support [https://budmain.org.ua/upload/filescatalog/items/0/06aff05bd8ef30d68330e7a787c0.pdf; https://www.liebherr.com/en-int/mining-equipment/equipment/mining-excavators/r9150-5392635]. Liebherr's PR 776 mining dozer is operational 24/7 at the Bystrinsky GOK copper mine in Siberia's Trans-Baikal Territory (Nornickel) [https://www.liebherr.com/shared/media/mining/brochures/job-reports/pr-776-bystrinsky/job-report-pr-776-russia-bystrinsky-mine.pdf].

---

## 2. Local Service Centers in Ulaanbaatar

### 2.1 Caterpillar — Barloworld Mongolia (formerly Wagner Asia)

Wagner Asia Equipment LLC was established in **1996** as the official Caterpillar dealer and was the **best-performing Cat dealer in the Eurasia/CIS region for seven consecutive years** [http://www.mongolianbusinessdatabase.com/base/companydetials?id=3449]. In **February 2020**, South African conglomerate Barloworld acquired 100% of Wagner Asia for **US$216.8 million**, creating Barloworld Mongolia [https://im-mining.com/2020/02/04/barloworld-makes-plans-establish-eurasia-equipment-unit/]. 

Barloworld Mongolia is headquartered in **Bayangol District, Ulaanbaatar**, with branches in Zaamar (Tuv province), Darkhan city, Tsogttsetsii and Khanbogd (Umnugovi province — the latter serving Oyu Tolgoi), and Zamiin-Uud (Dornogovi province). Approximately **600 employees** [https://linkedin.com/company/barloworldmongolia; https://rocketreach.co/wagner-asia-equipment-llc-profile_b5c803a1f42e346e].

The main UB shop has 100+ mechanics and 20+ supervisory staff; a field-service team for Mongolia-wide 24/7 dispatch with 50+ mechanics and 20+ delivery vehicles; 975 m² workshop with two overhead cranes (3.2T and 10T) and 9 specialized service lifts; 350 m² heavy-equipment wash bay; Cat contamination-control 4-Star certified; ISO 9001:2015 and OHSAS 18001:2007 accredited [https://www.barloworld.mn/en/service/main; https://www.barloworld.mn/en/service/field]. A Director-level role managed a **US$130 million parts-and-service after-sales business** covering nine departments: Parts/Warehouse, Component Rebuild Center, Contract Management, Warranty, Technical Services, Service Admin, Logistics, and Contamination Control [https://linkedin.com/in/randy-adler-5594282b]. The team has performed 70+ major rebuilds with 20+ years of mechanic tenure.

### 2.2 Komatsu — Transwest Mongolia

Transwest Mongolia LLC holds exclusive Komatsu dealership rights in Mongolia and is supported by **Sumitomo Corporation (Japan) and SMS Equipment (Canada)** — one of the largest Komatsu dealers worldwide. Address: No. 30, Erchim Khuch Street 1, Bayangol District, 29th Khoroo, Ulaanbaatar; +976-7575-9905 [https://www.transwest.mn/en-ca/about-us/]. Revenue ~US$28.9M; **203 employees** [https://rocketreach.co/transwest-mongolia-llc-profile_b5d8adf1f42e5ca4].

Service capability: over 120 specialists performing **300+ component rebuilds, 50+ machine assemblies, and 200+ on-call services annually** [https://www.transwest.mn/getmedia/55fdc3ac-a9dc-473f-8e07-4dd02340b8e0/Service-Catalogue.pdf]. Full engine and transmission overhaul of Komatsu diesel engines in UB; welding/fabrication shop with line-boring capability, a **500-ton vertical press** and a **100-ton H-beam press** [https://www.transwest.mn/en-ca/service-4a361fe3ec4f0cd803809746e23d4742/welding-and-machine-shop/]. A second service facility was commissioned in **Khanbogd soum, Umnugovi province in 2022** — on the door of Oyu Tolgoi [https://www.transwest.mn/en-ca/service/].

Komatsu opened a representative office in Mongolia (KLTD Ulaanbaatar) in 2025 [https://mn.linkedin.com/company/transwest-mongolia].

### 2.3 Volvo CE — No Verified Dedicated Dealer

Volvo CE's global dealer locator lists Mongolia as a covered country, but the dealer match page shows **no dealer location for Mongolia** [https://www.volvoce.com/global/en/global-dealer-locator/]. The only Volvo-branded entities found in Mongolia are:
- **Volvo Trucks Mongolia** (on-road, not construction equipment), operated by MNTTT Group, +976-7715-1534 [https://www.volvotrucks.mn/en-mn/]
- **Volvo Mongolia** trading office on Seoul Street offering the R100E 95-ton rigid hauler — appears to be a sales office/import arrangement rather than a full-service dealer [https://www.engineering10.com/MN/Ulaanbaatar/104317184885421/Volvo-Mongolia]

A single LinkedIn profile shows a "Service & Workshop Manager, Volvo Industrial Equipment, Mongolia" active in 2009–2011 [https://mn.linkedin.com/in/saimun-said-6796abb], suggesting Volvo CE had some in-country presence in that era, but no current official dealer is verifiable.

### 2.4 Implication

For a -40°C Mongolia fleet, **Caterpillar (Barloworld Mongolia) and Komatsu (Transwest Mongolia)** both have direct, full-service in-country support. **Volvo CE has effectively no dedicated dealer support** in Mongolia for mining-class equipment, and a direct inquiry to Volvo CE Asia would be warranted only if Volvo must be re-evaluated.

---

## 3. Parts Inventory for Rapid Repairs

### 3.1 Caterpillar / Barloworld

As of late 2025, Barloworld Mongolia stocks **approximately 36,000 part numbers totaling ~2,756,000 units** of parts across four Mongolian branch warehouses, maintained under ISO 9001 and Cat Contamination Control standards [https://www.linkedin.com/posts/barloworldmongolia_partsavailability-reliability-operationalexcellence-activity-7455421923053740032-dal1]. The parent Barloworld network provides access to 1.4 million genuine Cat parts via Parts.cat.com [https://barloworld-equipment.com/parts]. The UB Component Rebuild Center performs full rebuilds on torque converters, transmissions, differentials, wheel groups, gearboxes, and cylinders, with new, Reman, parts kits, salvaged, repaired, and remanufactured components — all warranty-backed [https://www.barloworld.mn/en/service/component].

### 3.2 Komatsu / Transwest

Transwest operates a parts warehouse in Ulaanbaatar with undercarriage and OEM all-makes coverage, plus a Track Management System for proactive inspections and a Track Press capable of pin/bushing replacement. The exclusive Distribution Agreement authorizes Transwest to represent Komatsu Ltd. on all equipment sales, parts, service, component remanufacture and rebuild [https://www.transwest.mn/en-ca/about-us/; https://www.transwest.mn/en-ca/parts-and-products/undercarriage/]. **All refurbishment/remanufacturing has been relocated from China/Japan into Mongolia** — a structural advantage for repair turnaround once components are in-country [https://www.mongolianminingjournal.com/a/73666].

### 3.3 Volvo CE

No dedicated in-Mongolia Volvo CE parts warehouse was identified. Volvo parts reach Mongolia via air-freight from Mumbai (**5–7 days DHL/FedEx**) through traders, or through Chinese brokers referencing Volvo model numbers (EC140–EC900) [https://partstrading.com/suppliers/volvo-parts-mongolia/; https://www.xmgtech.com/mn/volvo-model]. This is materially slower for urgent mining-fleet repairs than Barloworld or Transwest.

### 3.4 Spareparts.mn and Independent Suppliers

Independent suppliers such as Spareparts.mn (Ulaanbaatar, Sukhbaatar District, +976 8806 2850) supply spare parts for Komatsu and other mining equipment — useful as a secondary sourcing channel but not a Tier-1 OEM support route [https://spareparts.mn/].

---

## 4. Fuel Efficiency in Extreme Cold

### 4.1 Diesel Cold-Weather Penalty

At -40°C, diesel fuel must not cloud or gel. Mongolia applies the Customs Union fuel regulation **TR CU 013/2011** [http://www.mongolialaws.org/c-8210-0132011-tr-cu-about-requirements-to-automobile-and-aviation-gasoline-diesel-and-marine-fuel-jet-fuel-and-fuel-oil.aspx], and the applicable cold-fuel specification is **GOST R 55475-2013**, which defines:
- **Winter grade (З):** limiting filtration temperature -32°C or -38°C
- **Arctic grade (А):** limiting filtration temperature **-44°C, -48°C, or -52°C** [https://meganorms.com/gost-r-55475-2013.html; https://www.russiangost.com/p-59774-gost-r-55475-2013.aspx]

**At -40°C, winter-grade diesel will gel; you must source Arctic-grade fuel (CFPP ≤ -44°C or lower), or blend with kerosene/cold-flow additives.** A 2021 Russian industrial batch reached -65°C application temperature [https://exa.ai/library/publication/97d7x7gkxkn]. Russian-supplied arctic diesel therefore covers -40°C operation *if it keeps flowing*.

### 4.2 Mongolia's Fuel Supply Vulnerability

Mongolia imports approximately **95% of its petroleum products from Russia**, with Russian exports supplying virtually all of Mongolia's diesel [https://www.intellinews.com/hit-indirectly-by-sanctions-mongolia-struggles-to-find-workarounds-351043/]. Western sanctions on Russian energy companies and banks have created payment difficulties and supply uncertainty, complicating procurement of winter-grade diesel. Mongolia secured an agreement for stable **winter diesel deliveries from October**, while holding ~85,600 t of diesel ≈ **21 days of national supply** (implied ~4,076 t/day consumption) and diversifying to China/South Korea via slow rail-gauge transfers [https://mn.ibtimes.com/mongolia-expands-fuel-supply-beyond-russia-china-south-korea-1812481].

### 4.3 Manufacturer Cold-Weather Fuel Strategies

- **Caterpillar** addresses fuel gelling with a "Fuel Blender" option on the 6040 cold-weather package [https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20210601-35dac-75766], allowing blending of #1 and #2 diesel to achieve required CFPP. Auto-warm-up, cold-start block heaters, arctic hydraulic oil, and antifreeze to -50°C/-58°F on the 824 Wheel Dozer eliminate cold-idling waste [https://www.fabickcat.com/new-equipment/824-wheel-dozer/].

- **Komatsu ThermaStart** autonomous idle management on Komatsu 830E, field-tested through Canadian tundra at -30°C, eliminates unnecessary idling and warm-up cycles via continuous monitoring of block temperature, battery voltage, and air pressure [https://www.roscomining.com/post/thermastart-komatsu-830e-cold-weather]. For oil-sands/bitumen transport, the 980E routes engine exhaust through the dump body to keep ore from freezing [https://www.komatsu.jp/en/-/media/home/aboutus/innovation/technology/techreport/2017/en/180330_06e.pdf].

- **Komatsu 930E-5** delivers up to **5% less fuel** than its predecessor via on-demand cooling [https://www.constructionequipment.com/earthmoving/rigid-frame-trucks-off-highway/product/10752402/komatsu-komatsu-930e-5-haul-truck]. Komatsu 930E AC drive is documented as "more efficient, offers better operating characteristics and is more cost effective than a comparable DC powertrain" [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Komatsu_930E].

- **Volvo CE** operator guidance: drain fuel/water separators nightly, fill fuel tanks nightly, regenerate DPF before cold shutdown, swap to arctic-grade engine/hydraulic oils [https://www.volvoce.com/en-ca/discover/guides-and-advice/2021/diesel-engine-dos-and-donts-to-prep-for-winter-season/]. Volvo's standard V-ACT D16J on the A60 carries a fuel-efficiency claim of "up to 15% more fuel efficiency" vs. prior generation [https://www.volvoce.com/united-states/en-us/products/articulated-haulers/a60/]. Volvo's EC350E claims up to 9% better fuel efficiency than its prior generation [https://www.volvoce.com/united-states/en-us/products/excavators/ec350e/] — unproven in Mongolian -40°C service.

### 4.4 General Cold-Weather Fuel Economy Penalty

Industry data shows fleet fuel economy drops materially in extreme cold due to increased warm-up time and fluid viscosity, tire pressure drops, and increased aerodynamic drag (a 10°F drop raises drag ~2%, ~1% loss in MPG per 2% drag increase) [https://www.elementfleet.com/insights-and-resources/insights/blogs/fleet-fuel-management-how-cold-temperatures-affect-fuel-economy; https://www.freightliner.com/blog-and-newsletters/how-adverse-weather-affects-fuel-economy/]. Light-duty vehicles lose ~15% MPG at -7°C vs. 25°C, and up to ~24% on short 3–4 mile trips. Heavy diesel on long highway runs drops ~5–10%, but frequent cold starts and idling make the effective impact much worse. Winter-blend fuels (No. 1-D/kerosene blend) have lower BTU content [https://restservice.epri.com/publicdownload/TR-104843/0/Product; https://www.atbs.com/post/diesel-winterization].

---

## 5. Operator and Technician Training Programs for Mongolian Workers

### 5.1 Caterpillar / Wagner-Barloworld

Wagner Asia established the **Wagner Training Institute (WTI)** in ~2001 in Ulaanbaatar. Independent commentary states: *"Wagner Asia's training model set the standard for vocational education in the entire country of Mongolia"* [https://wagnerequipment.com/wagner-training-institute/wti-staff/]. Instructors were certified through the Caterpillar Instructor Accreditation Program (CIAP).

The apprentice program: ~30 students per intake, ~150 Mongolian technicians trained across six intakes in five years, in partnership with the Mongolian Korean Technical College; **100% graduate employment** [https://news.mn/en/12137/]. Customers send mechanics on paid **10-month theory+practice courses** (e.g., Energy Resources for the Ukhaa Khudag mine), covering Caterpillar systems, service-manual dismantling/assembly, and ET-software diagnostics [https://en.energyresources.mn/post/179240]. A Competency-Based Training system was implemented with German consultancy support, 2011–2013 [https://vetp.mn/uploaded/documents/2023/October/finalreport-mng-edu].

Caterpillar's Mining Technology Academy (MTA) offers eLearning, Instructor-Led Training (ILT), and Operator Training in three levels: Level I (<3 years), Level II (3+ years), and Competent Operator evaluation [https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20250714-13ab0-e7282; https://www.catoperatortraining.com/pages/instructor-led-training]. Barloworld Mongolia has in-country accredited Caterpillar instructors (e.g., Batbayar Dorjsuren) [https://linkedin.com/in/batbayar-dorjsuren-161b51b9]. Barloworld staff are sent to Caterpillar's Tinaja Hills Demonstration & Learning Center in Green Valley, AZ for MineStar Terrain and product training [https://www.linkedin.com/posts/nymbaatar-altansukh-a86b59199_caterpillar-minestar-minestarterrain-activity-7473644063595048960-kdc9].

### 5.2 Komatsu / Transwest Mongolia Technical Institute

Transwest Mongolia Technical Institute (TMTI) operates as Mongolia's dedicated Komatsu training institute. In **February 2026** TMTI delivered advanced hydraulic-systems training on Komatsu 930E-4SE electric-drive dump trucks to **Oyu Tolgoi's Heavy Equipment Maintenance Department** in combined classroom and practical format, in Mongolian-language and English instruction [https://www.linkedin.com/posts/transwest-mongolia_komatsu930e-oyutolgoillc-komatsu930e-activity-7428957197641895936-Bo-1].

In **June–July 2025**, Transwest co-delivered Komatsu PC7000-11D Technical Training with Komatsu Germany Mining (KGM) at Nariin Sukhait Mine — a 10-day combined program integrating theory and practice [https://www.linkedin.com/posts/chinzorig-ganbat_were-proud-to-announce-the-successful-completion-activity-7355832096709337089-e_Gv]. Transwest opened a new Technical Institute in **2024** with Komatsu Ltd., Sumitomo Corporation, SMS Equipment Inc., and Komatsu Germany/America [https://www.transwest.mn/en-ca/news-resources/news/2024/transwest-mongolia-company-s-15th-anniversary-ceremony-a-success/]. The training program integrates Australian curriculum, Komatsu's training systems, and locally designed modules [https://www.bus-ex.com/article/transwest-mongolia-llc-forging-local-excellence-through-innovation-skills-green-technology]. Komatsu Academy offers self-paced online modules and instructor-led live coaching [https://www.komatsu.com/en-us/services-and-support/training-programs].

### 5.3 Immersive Technologies / Oyu Tolgoi Simulation

Oyu Tolgoi (Rio Tinto) invested in the **PRO3 simulator from Immersive Technologies** in 2011, initially supporting Komatsu haul-truck operator training, with a five-year gold support program and Custom Mine Site [https://www.immersivetechnologies.com/news/news2011/news_2011_21.htm].

### 5.4 Mongolia Polytechnic / German-Mongolian Cooperation (2025)

A "Mining Machinery Operation Technician" program at the Polytechnic College affiliated with the University of Technology in Ömnögovi province is delivered via public-private partnership with Germany's Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development and Ministry of Education. More than 80% of students are from Umnögovi, with blended learning — interns and learn-while-working placements at mining employers [https://mcpg.mn/en/9281/].

### 5.5 South Gobi Underground Mass Mining Institute (2025)

Launched in **March 2025** by Rio Tinto and the University of Queensland, the South Gobi Underground Mass Mining Institute is based at Oyu Tolgoi with a 2025 cohort of 28 participants. The 2026 curriculum will open to local and international mining companies, focusing on underground mining, geotechnics, and mining engineering [https://www.australianmining.com.au/rio-tinto-debuts-world-class-training-program-at-oyu-tolgoi/].

---

## 6. Russian-Made and CIS Alternatives

### 6.1 BelAZ Product Range and Mongolian Footprint

BelAZ is the largest supplier of mining dump trucks in the CIS and offers the broadest cold-rated product line:

| Model | Payload | Engine | Cold Rating |
|---|---|---|---|
| BelAZ-75710 | 450 t | 2× MTU DD 16V4000 | -50/+50°C |
| BelAZ-75605 | 360 t | 18-cyl, 3,300 hp | -50/+50°C |
| BelAZ-75306 | 220 t | Cummins QSK 60 | -50/+50°C |
| BelAZ-7513A/75135 | 130–136 t | MTU DD 12V4000 | -50/+50°C |
| BelAZ-7558B Series | 90 t | Cummins KTA 38-C (preheat) | -50/+50°C |
| BelAZ-7513R (robotic) | 130–136 t | electric drive | -50/+50°C |

Sources: [https://belaz.by/upload/iblock/651/BELAZ_75710.pdf; https://belaz.by/upload/iblock/d44/BELAZ_75306.pdf; https://belaz.by/upload/iblock/3a9/BELAZ_7513A.pdf; https://belaz.by/upload/iblock/5ce/BELAZ_7558_English.pdf; https://belaz.by/upload/iblock/a29/_75605.pdf; https://belaz.by/upload/iblock/589/BELAZ_7513R.pdf]

BelAZ has also piloted **LNG (liquefied natural gas) cryogenic fuel systems** on dump trucks, intending to reduce diesel dependence in Russian coal regions like Kuzbass [https://www.matec-conferences.org/articles/matecconf/pdf/2019/46/matecconf_ispcime18_03002.pdf]. Specific fuel consumption (SFC) at nominal power is **196–201 g/kWh** (BelAZ-75710: 198; BelAZ-75605: 196; BelAZ-7513A: 201), competitive with modern Western mining diesel-electric drives (typically 190–200 g/kWh).

### 6.2 United BelAZ Machinery (UBM) — Official Mongolian Distributor

**United BelAZ Machinery LLC (UBM)** is the official BelAZ distributor in Mongolia, established **2012** to resolve parts/service complaints from earlier grey-imports [https://ikon.mn/n/272t]. UBM has:
- **160 employees**, of whom 130 are mining machinery engineers and technicians
- A centralized parts and tire warehouse in Ulaanbaatar and Umnugovi province worth **16 billion MNT** (~US$4.5M)
- Belarusian factory specialists permanently assigned to Mongolia (e.g., L.Ya. Slobodsky) [https://ikon.mn/n/272t]

**About 200 BelAZ vehicles are in operation in Mongolia**, with payload classes of 30, 45, 55, 130, and 220 t [https://eng.belta.by/economics/view/belaz-to-ship-3m-worth-of-haul-trucks-to-mongolia-103863-2017/; https://www.belarus.by/en/business/business-news/belarusian-belaz-ships-first-bulldozer-to-mongolia_i_110184.html]. 35 haul trucks were shipped in 2019, with about 40 planned in 2020. The 130 t BelAZ-75135 is the sweet spot for mid-size Mongolian mines — 17 trucks delivered in three batches to the Erdenes Tavan Tolgoi consortium "укомплектованные с учетом экстремальных климатических условий пустыни Гоби" (equipped for the extreme climatic conditions of the Gobi Desert) [https://minprom.gov.by/belazy-serii-7513-budut-rabotat-v-pustyne-gobi/]. BelAZ's first bulldozer was shipped to Mongolia in 2020 as evidence of expanding product line beyond haul trucks.

United BelAZ Machinery sends Mongolian specialists to the BelAZ factory in Zhodino, Belarus, for operations and service training, with documented training groups returning from Zhodino [https://news.mn/en/135983/].

### 6.3 Mongolia-Russia Trade Context

- Mongolia imports roughly 28% of goods from Russia and **depends on Russia for approximately 95% of its petroleum products** [https://www.trtworld.com/asia/mongolia-is-feeling-weight-of-western-sanctions-on-russia-over-ukraine-war-18214964].
- A December 2024 interim trade agreement between the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) and Mongolia was signed [https://russiancouncil.ru/en/analytics-and-comments/analytics/russia-and-mongolia-forging-stronger-trade-relations/]. February 2026 saw further expansion via Mongolia-Russia Business Forum with 70+ Mongolian businesses meeting 100+ Russian businesses [https://thediplomat.com/2026/02/with-speaker-uchrals-trip-mongolia-and-russia-look-to-expand-economic-links/].
- US/EU sanctions on Russia have created indirect payment difficulties for Mongolia and secondary-sanction risk deterring direct air links [https://www.intellinews.com/hit-indirectly-by-sanctions-mongolia-struggles-to-find-workarounds-351043/; https://iz.ru/en/node/1848658]. For BelAZ mining equipment specifically, no direct sanctions impact on BelAZ itself was identified, but the broader Russia-CIS logistics environment is uncertain.
- China dominates Mongolia's construction-machinery import market at **65–70% by value** (2026), with Japanese OEMs (Komatsu, Hitachi) holding the large mining segment and second-hand imports at ~20% [https://www.ibicrossborder.com/upload/ai_report/en/html/20260718003522-f2bb78fbbc.html]. Chinese brands (Sany, XCMG, Yuchai) are gaining ground at the small-to-medium scale and at government-owned mines like Erdenet [https://projects.gbreports.com/mongolia-mining-2024/equipment-and-technology-maturing-in-a-realm-of-unpredictability].
- For Mongolia's fixed mining equipment market, the top-five manufacturers (Metso, Sandvik, FLSmidth, Caterpillar, Weir Group) collectively command ~65% of revenue (2026) [https://www.marknteladvisors.com/research-library/mongolia-fixed-mining-equipment-market.html].

---

## 7. Side-by-Side Comparison Table

| Criterion | Caterpillar | Komatsu | Volvo CE | BelAZ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Cold rating (-40°C)** | Standard -18°C; with Cold Weather Package + arctic options rated to -32°C; -50°C fluids available | Factory -50°C achievable with preheating; -25°C threshold for normal operation | No factory -40°C rating; arctic oils + cold prep recommended | **Factory -50/+50°C** rated across product line |
| **Ulaanbaatar dealer** | Barloworld Mongolia (since 1996; 600 staff; 5 branches) | Transwest Mongolia (exclusive; 203 staff); KLTD office 2025 | No clear CE mining dealer; Volvo Trucks via MNTTT only | United BelAZ Machinery (since 2012; 160 staff; 130 technical) |
| **Workshop capacity** | 975 m² UB shop, 9 specialized lifts, Component Rebuild Center | 120+ specialists, 300+ rebuilds/yr, 500-ton press, Khanbogd facility | None in Mongolia; air-freight from India/China 5–7 days | 2,289 m² UB service base; parts warehouse 16B MNT; mine-site support |
| **Parts inventory** | **36,000 SKUs / ~2.76 M units** across 4 Mongolian branches (ISO 9001) | UB warehouse; all reman relocated to Mongolia; 200+ on-site calls/yr | No Mongolian inventory; aftermarket via Mumbai traders | 16B MNT centralized warehouse in UB + Umnugovi |
| **Fuel efficiency** | Auto-warm-up, fuel blender, -50°C coolant, fuel heaters | ThermaStart eliminates idle waste on 830E; 930E AC drive up to 5% better; 980E heated-body exhaust | Up to 15% A60 vs. prior gen; unproven in Mongolia | SFC 196–201 g/kWh at nominal power; LNG pilot available |
| **Operator training** | WTI (since 2001); ~150 technicians trained; national benchmark; Mining Technology Academy | TMTI + new Technical Institute (2024); co-delivered with Komatsu Germany; Mongolian-language instruction | None in-country | Factory training at Zhodino; 130 Mongolian engineers/technicians |
| **Mining fleet proof** | Cat 6060/7495 at Oyu Tolgoi; 773E at Ulz | 28× 930E-4SE at Oyu Tolgoi since 2012; HD1500-8 at Erdenet (+7.9% volume, -5.8% cost) | None found | 200+ units; Erdenet, Tavan Tolgoi (17× 75135 Gobi-configured) |
| **Sanction/regional risk** | None | None | None | Secondary-sanction risk via Russia-CIS banking |

---

## 8. Recommended Strategy for a Mongolia Mining Fleet at -40°C

1. **Haul trucks — primary fleet:** Specify **Komatsu 930E-5/930E-5SE** (290 t) or **HD1500-8** (142 t) with full Cold Weather Packages. The Komatsu 930E has the strongest documented in-Mongolia track record (Oyu Tolgoi's 28 trucks operating since 2012), and Transwest Mongolia provides UB + Khanbogd service coverage plus the 2024 Technical Institute for technician development [https://en.eot.mn/open-pit-mine]. The Cat 793F/789D (with coolant to -50°C) combined with Barloworld's 36,000-SKU inventory and Component Rebuild Center is the equally viable alternative.

2. **Excavators:** Specify **Cat 6040/6050** or **Komatsu PC4000-6** with the factory cold-weather package (coolant/oil/hydraulic heaters, cab pre-heater, ~50 kW shore power). Choose based on which haul truck brand you select to standardize the dealer relationship. Cat's 6040 cold-weather package documentation is the most detailed found [https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20260211-22a73-3be06]. Komatsu's PC4000 has the HYDRONIC independent cab heater — a genuine operational advantage for -40°C shift starts [https://www.manualslib.com/manual/3641219/Komatsu-Pc4000-6.html?page=95]. For excavator alignment with BelAZ trucks, **Liebherr R 9150** with the Arctic Package (validated at ALROSA's -55°C mine) is the highest-confidence European alternative.

3. **Exclude Volvo CE for primary mining fleet duty** unless Volvo CE Region Asia appoints an official Mongolian dealer with a bonded parts warehouse. The absence from the dealer locator [https://www.volvoce.com/global/en/global-dealer-locator/], the 5–7-day third-party parts lead time, and the lack of documented -40°C package make it unsuitable.

4. **Russian alternatives — selective supplement:** Consider **BelAZ-75135** (130 t) for cost-efficient auxiliary haul capacity or fleet diversification. UBM provides a 16B MNT local parts warehouse, factory training pipeline, and short supply chain from Belarus. The 200+ BelAZ units already operating in Mongolia demonstrate field viability. However, retain a Western service partner for high-value powertrain and hydraulic rebuilds. Note BelAZ does not supply excavators.

5. **Fuel procurement:** Contract **Arctic-grade diesel meeting GOST R 55475-2013 with limiting filtration temperature ≤ -44°C** (grade А) [https://meganorms.com/gost-r-55475-2013.html]. Given the 95% Russian fuel dependency and 2026 export-control disruptions, budget for fuel-blender preheaters (Cat option) or kerosene blending as backup. Procure low-temperature engine oil (0W-40 or SAE 5W-30 synthetic per manufacturer charts), coolant protected to -50°C, and battery blankets.

6. **Site infrastructure:** Budget for **external 400V three-phase shore power** at the fleet parking area to energize the ~50 kW pre-heating systems overnight — this is the single largest lever on cold-start reliability and fuel economy [https://s7d2.scene7.com/is/content/Caterpillar/CM20210601-35dac-75766].

7. **Training pipeline:** Build on Transwest Mongolia Technical Institute + Wagner Training Institute / Barloworld Mining Technology Academy pathways for operator and technician development. Partner with Rio Tinto's South Gobi Underground Mass Mining Institute and the Ömnögovi Polytechnic "Mining Machinery Operation Technician" program for long-term workforce pipeline.

8. **Spare-parts SLA:** Negotiate consignment-stock contracts with Barloworld Mongolia and Transwest Mongolia for the highest-failure-rate SKUs (hydraulic hoses, undercarriage components, fuel/water separator elements, coolant hoses). Mongolia's landlocked logistics (Tianjin port congestion routinely strands ~6,000 containers with delays up to three months; logistics add 15–30% to product cost) [https://projects.gbreports.com/mongolia-mining-2024/equipment-and-technology-maturing-in-a-realm-of-unpredictability] make any 5–7-day air-freight cycle from Mumbai (Volvo) unacceptable for primary mining-truck downtime.

---

## 9. Key Caveats and Uncertainties

- **BelAZ TCO data:** BelAZ figures (200+ units, 16B MNT warehouse) come from 2020–2021 sources and may have changed; no audited 2024–2026 TCO comparison was found.
- **Komatsu reliability degradation at -40°C:** The 2–6× failure-rate increase at -25°C noted for Komatsu D-375A/A5 dozers in northern Russia was not numerically characterized at -40°C; specific failure rates at -40°C on Komatsu 930E/980E were not found.
- **Volvo CE status:** Volvo CE's current Mongolian status is inferred from absence of dealer-locator data; a direct inquiry to Volvo CE Asia is warranted if Volvo must be re-evaluated.
- **Mongolia diesel winter-blend availability in 2024–2026:** The Russian supply chain dominates but Western sanctions on Russian banks/energy companies create payment risk that could affect winter-grade availability at South Gobi operations.
- **No TCO comparison:** Total cost of ownership comparisons across the four OEMs for a -40°C Mongolian mining fleet were not available; recommendations are based on cold-weather capability, service footprint, parts reach, and workforce development pipeline rather than lifecycle cost models.

# Adaptive Input Systems for Musicians with Hand Tremor in DAW Environments

## Premise corrections before any synthesis

Three of the brief's central premises cannot be verified in primary sources and must be flagged before the comparison can proceed.

**Ableton Live does not ship a tremor filter.** Its "Velocity" MIDI effect is a memoryless per-note amplitude remapper, not a temporal smoother or 4–12 Hz rejection stage. The Velocity device exposes `Range`, `Lowest`, `Out Hi`, `Out Low`, `Operation`, `Mode`, `Random`, and `Drive` controls, with three out-of-range behaviors: **Clip** (clamp), **Gate** (silently remove notes below `Lowest`, LED flashes when blocked), and **Fixed** (map to `Out Hi`) (https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-midi-effect-reference/; https://obedia.com/how-to-use-the-velocity-midi-effect-in-ableton-live/). Gate mode is the only tremor-adjacent mechanism in the stock device, and it is a crude amplitude threshold: a soft unintended touch is deleted — and so is an intentionally soft *pp* note. Live 12's only literal "smoothing" lives inside Max for Live modulators (`Smoothing Type` toggle plus `Smoothing Rise`/`Fall` sliders, "from 0 to 1000 milliseconds"), and it acts on modulation curves, not note velocity (https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/max-for-live-devices/). The Max for Live Velocity Shaper MIDI Tool is similarly offline, applying a breakpoint envelope to a *selection* of notes (https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/midi-tools/). A 2009 user thread documents the Gate workaround: "use gate mode in the Velocity device, and set the 'lowest' slider to 25, 30, etc. basically adjust it til it no longer picks up the quiet notes. only the velocities over 25, 35 etc will make it through" (https://forum.ableton.com/viewtopic.php?t=120139). Live 12's accessibility additions (screen-reader support, high-contrast theme, Tab navigation, Speak Minimum and Maximum Slider Values, Speak Menu Commands) target vision-impaired and keyboard-only users, not tremor (https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/accessibility-options-in-live/; https://help.ableton.com/hc/en-us/articles/11550373507868-Accessibility-in-Live-Overview).

**Logic Pro's Smart Controls contain no tremor compensation.** Apple's user guide describes Smart Controls only as "on-screen controls" that adapt plug-in and channel-strip parameters for a selected track: "Adjusting a single screen control can change one or more parameters for the track's channel strip, instrument, and effect plug-ins" (https://support.apple.com/guide/logicpro/smart-controls-overview-lgcp7e59f24b/mac). The Logic Pro accessibility VPAT (2024) confirms that accessibility is delegated to macOS-level features: VoiceOver, Switch Control, keyboard navigation, Zoom, Sticky Keys ("a series of single key presses to be interpreted as a multiple keystroke combination"), and Slow Keys (https://support.apple.com/content/dam/edam/applecare/images/en_US/otherassets/accessibility/vpat_logic_pro_2024.pdf). The Logic stock `Tremolo` and `Vibrato` controls are audio effects with `Depth`/`Speed`/`Sync` parameters (https://help.apple.com/pdf/logicpromac-effects/en_US/logic-pro-mac-effects-user-guide.pdf) — the opposite of tremor suppression. The closest genuine assistive Logic deployment found is a University of Milan PhD project that combined Logic Pro + Max + an eye tracker + micro-muscular sensors for a musician restricted to finger, toe, and eye movement (https://air.unimi.it/retrieve/a7a83c36-2310-4105-b143-57edcab7f0f8/phd_unimi_R13911_3.pdf). Logic-side remediation for tremor therefore consists of (a) external hardware with their own anti-tremor firmware, (b) host-level assistive tools like SteadyMouse on Windows or built-in macOS pointer smoothing (Mouse Keys, Sticky Keys, Slow Keys), and (c) tracks of pre-quantized MIDI rather than live performance capture.

**SteadyMouse 2 is the only one of the three performing genuine tremor rejection — but at the OS cursor layer, not the MIDI layer.** It detects and removes shaking motion "before it reaches your cursor" and blocks accidental clicks (https://www.steadymouse.com/; VA TRM entry https://www.oit.va.gov/Services/TRM/ToolPage.aspx?tid=11407; manual dated January 2026: https://www.steadymouse.com/manual/). Documented features: seven filter sets — *Allegro* (default medium), *Feather* (snappiest, formerly called "Gaming"), *Adagio* (heavy, laggy but powerful), *Classic* (v1 heritage), *Artistry* (smooth curves for drawing), *Laggy* (extreme tremor), *Steadicam* (new in 2.8.2.0, for camera-style stabilization); a filter-strength slider with the explicit tuning procedure "Start with mouse speed below ten percent and filter strength around 95%… then decrease strength until tremor just begins to reappear"; click-duration gating that drops mouse clicks shorter than a configurable threshold (distinguishing accidental taps from intentional ones by hold time); an *Icon Targeting* snap-to-target mode activated by double-tapping a modifier key; auto-disable of Windows "Enhanced Pointer Precision" (because it "actually degrades precision"); and a Num-Lock (or Scroll-Lock) global on/off toggle. SteadyMouse is **Windows-only**; a Mac port is acknowledged as "extremely difficult" and not yet released. It cannot distinguish intentional vibrato-like mid-pitch MIDI modulation from involuntary 4–7 Hz oscillation because, at the cursor layer, it has no notion of musical intent — that distinction has to happen further up the stack, in the DAW or a custom MIDI effect. It is also listed as an assistive device by the International Essential Tremor Organization (https://essentialtremor.org/assistive-devices/steadymouse-hand-tremor-mouse-accessibility-software/).

The structural consequence is that the three filtering layers are disjoint: a MIDI keyboard performance — tremor-contaminated velocities, duplicated note triggers, wobbly pitch-bend — bypasses SteadyMouse entirely. Conversely, Live's Velocity device and Logic's parameter mapping graphs touch MIDI data but are blind to gesture frequency. Intentional vibrato in DAW practice (pitch-bend CC, aftertouch, or mouse-drawn automation) lives in neither filter's default path. **No commercially documented DAW feature performs frequency-selective separation of pathological tremor from expressive gesture at the MIDI layer.**

## The signal problem: pathological tremor and vibrato occupy the same band

The brief's claim that "pathological tremor (4–12 Hz)" can be cleanly separated from musical expression techniques is not supported by the acoustic/motor-control literature.

| Phenomenon | Frequency | Extent / character | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| PD rest tremor | 4–6 Hz (some sources 3–6 Hz) | Action-independent | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5573102/; https://parkinsons.org/symptoms/tremor; https://www.racgp.org.au/getattachment/4b03a304-f3a5-4571-917f-ee52f594808e/Classification-and-treatment-of-tremor.aspx |
| Essential tremor (action) | 4–12 Hz | Kinetic/postural | https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/neurology/articles/10.3389/fneur.2021.684835/full |
| ET measured at rest (EMG) | ~5–8 Hz | Identical to vibrato band | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5573102/ |
| Enhanced physiological tremor | 6–12 Hz | Normal | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5573102/ |
| Western lyric vocal vibrato | 5–8 Hz, sinusoidal | < ±1.0 semitone (~±6%), low variability | https://pubs.aip.org/asa/jasa/article/130/1/EL1/907816/Vibrato-and-tremor-extent-spectrum-Algorithm-and |
| Violin vibrato (voluntary) | ~5–7 Hz dominant, individual-specific | "Almost isometric" flexor-extensor alternation; persistent rhythmic EMG groups | https://exa.ai/library/publication/ddgkqcy2fr5 |
| Primary bowing tremor (pathological, violinists) | 4.7–6.7 Hz | Wrist flexion-extension; onset ~43 years | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4053556/ |
| Secondary task-specific bowing tremor post-temporal-lobectomy | ~7 Hz | Right-arm-only; coherent with wrist EMG | https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4117185/ |
| General pathological tremor band | 3–15 Hz | Used as spectral envelope for tremor suppression filters | http://www.neuralrehabilitation.org/projects/tremor/Documents/deliverables/TREMOR%20D4.1%20update.pdf |
| Voice wow / tremor / flutter | 0–2 / 2–10 / 10–20 Hz | Modulogram bands | https://www.acoustics.asn.au/conference_proceedings/ICA2010/cdrom-ICA2010/papers/p42.pdf |

The arithmetic of the overlap (made explicit in one panel's analysis): the vibrato band 5–8 Hz spans 3 Hz; the ET band 4–12 Hz spans 8 Hz; their intersection = 5–8 Hz = 100% of the vibrato band inside the ET band. The PD rest band 4–6 Hz vs vibrato gives an intersection of 5–6 Hz = 33% of the vibrato band and 50% of the PD band. The EMG study that measured ET at rest at 5–8 Hz is *identical* to the vibrato band. Frequency-domain filtering therefore cannot separate them.

The strongest single physiological line of evidence that vibrato and tremor share motor machinery: after a violin vibrato run stops, persisting EMG rhythmic groups *accelerate into the 8–12 Hz physiological tremor range*. This suggests vibrato is built on the same oscillatory machinery as tremor, not on a separable voluntary system.

What does separate them, per the acoustics literature, is *regularity*: vocal tremor has "similar rate and extent averages" to vibrato "but the variability is greater" (Ramig & Shipp, cited in the JASA extent-spectrum paper); a single-subject acoustic/EMG case study of one person with both vibrato and essential voice tremor found sung (voluntary) modulation was slower, more prominent, and *more regular*, "suggesting differences in the neural bases" (https://exa.ai/library/publication/3fjs73lrd3d). A clinical study found tremor analysis using frequency alone "is not sufficient to differentiate tremor in ET and PD" (mean frequencies 5.29 ± 1.18 Hz PD vs 5.97 ± 1.1 Hz ET: https://www.scielo.br/j/anp/a/FNMcgRcwCDZgzgfCc3qPLwn/?lang=en); the two are better separated by *frequency tolerance* (temporal stability of the oscillation) than by frequency itself (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4293424/). Any DAW-layer tremor filter would therefore need regularity/context features, not a notch filter — and would still risk rejecting a performer's genuinely regular, intentional vibrato.

## HCI research on gesture rejection: the Voight-Kampff Machine as the closest analogue

The cleanest piece of HCI work on thresholding tremor-like vs. intentional motion is Taranta, Maslych, Ghamandi, and LaViola's **Voight-Kampff Machine (VKM)**, CHI 2022 (https://cs.ucf.edu/~jjl/pubs/Taranta2022.pdf). VKM is not a tremor filter; it is a *rejection-threshold selector* for custom-gesture recognizers that must decide which continuous-stream inputs to accept as gestures vs. treat as non-gesture noise. The relevance to tremor compensation is direct: any system that filters "the wobble" must decide where the wobble ends and the gesture begins.

Key quantitative findings:

- VKM is the **only threshold-selection technique that consistently achieves high accuracy across four input device types** (pen, mouse, 3D-depth, IMU) on the high-activity gesture datasets tested.
- Quoting Taranta et al.: "loose boundaries can lead to high false positive rates and degrade user experience"; "eliminating false positives is more important than eliminating false negatives" (citing Katsuragawa et al., reference [21] in their paper). A false positive in this domain is *the same failure mode* as a tremor spike passing through to a note — the system misfires on involuntary input.
- VKM's technical contribution is a synthetic-data technique ("Mincer") that produces **negative samples near the gesture boundary**, yielding tighter rejection thresholds than prior splicing techniques (which VKM's authors show are appropriate only for *low-activity* data).
- Empirical tuning parameters reported: training-set size shrinks the threshold (more positive examples → tighter cut); gesture-production variability widens it (gaming/performance contexts are more variable than desktop data-collection contexts, sometimes substantially so — Taranta et al. cite a finding that the same gesture set can have different variability across applications).

VKM is, in effect, an existence proof that selective tremor rejection is tractable — but it is bench-tested on drawn gestures, not expressive MIDI parameters. Mapping this to vibrato preservation would require representing both the tremor and the vibrato in the same feature space and tuning VKM to prefer the more periodic of the two.

The closest audio-side analogue is Boeck, Widmer et al., "Local Group Delay based Vibrato and Tremolo Suppression for Onset Detection," ISMIR 2013 (https://www.cp.jku.at/research/papers/Boeck_Widmer_Ismir_2013.pdf). Their weighting of spectral-flux onset detection by local group delay reduces false onsets caused by vibrato/tremolo energy peaks by **up to 50%** across three corpora: 25,927 mixed onsets, 7,677 violin onsets, and 1,448 opera-singer onsets. Note that this is the *opposite* direction from what a tremor user needs — they want vibrato-style modulation to *pass through*, but the algorithm is built to treat both as spurious onsets. Reusing this for tremor accommodation would require inverting the cost function.

For EMG-level discrimination (closer to what a MIDI exoskeleton might exploit), the Missouri group showed that the **frequency of EMG modulation in ET shifts when voluntary motion is initiated** vs. when the patient is merely holding posture — a "tremor frequency based filter" using an STFT-derived switch achieved partial voluntary-motion preservation that pure low-pass filters damaged (http://vigir.ee.missouri.edu/~gdesouza/Research/Conference_CDs/BioRob_2012/files/0452.pdf). The same group's "optimal digital filtering for tremor suppression" introduced an "equalizer" framework for joystick teleoperation, validated both on artificially-induced vibration and a Parkinson's subject, with the source code archived (https://nemours.elsevierpure.com/en/publications/optimal-digital-filtering-for-tremor-suppression/). A 2025 *Scientific Reports* paper on adaptive tremor-suppression for a smart pen (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-14196-5) compares Fx-LMS, Fx-NLMS, Fx-LMS/NLMS hybrid, RLS, and Kalman filtering on real PD signals from the NewHandPD dataset; they report that **RLS achieves the lowest mean squared error, but the Kalman Filter converges approximately eight times faster** — relevant because convergence speed translates directly to user-perceived latency during composition.

The infrastructure for finer-grained rejection therefore exists — VKM, the STFT tremor-frequency switch, the Kalman smart pen — but no peer-reviewed paper has demonstrated it inside a DAW MIDI pipeline. The cognitive load of training such a system per-user, per-session, would be non-trivial.

## Documented case studies of musicians with movement disorders in/adjacent to DAWs

**Samuel Smith — Parkinson's, AI-mediated workflow (2026).** The most thoroughly documented recent case is London-based singer-songwriter Samuel Smith, diagnosed with Parkinson's in 2020, who released *The Art of Letting Go* in 2026 (https://fortune.com/2026/05/30/parkinsons-ai-music-humming-demos/; https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/05/30/world/ai-helped-musician-with-parkinsons-finish-new-album-when-he-could-no-longer-play-guitar/). Smith hums melodies into a phone, uploads them to Suno and Udio, and edits the AI-generated demos into the final album's instrumental plan. He reports needing **"50, 100, 150 attempts"** per demo before producing something usable (https://aitoolsobserver.com/hub/ai-for-musicians-with-disabilities-inside-samuel-smiths-workflow-with-suno-and-udio/). Critically, the AI demos were not used as the final masters — they were translation layers between his humming and session musicians. This sidesteps the tremor-vs-intent problem entirely by removing the tremor-bearing input modality, but the 50–150-attempt loop is a flow-destroying overhead by construction.

**Kira — Essential Tremor, DBS.** A touring musician profiled by PMD Alliance in December 2025 (https://www.pmdalliance.org/2025/12/03/touring-musician-kiras-essential-tremor-journey/) reports that prior to deep-brain stimulation she "couldn't play her guitar, and times when she couldn't even get on stage," and that she historically self-medicated with alcohol because prescriptions failed. After a 30 October 2024 DBS procedure, "Immediately, I saw improvement in my right hand. I cried on the operating table as I watched a hand that I felt so disconnected with… show a steadiness." This is a hardware/neurosurgical remediation case, not a DAW-software one — but it documents the magnitude of the symptom set software systems are working against.

**Valerie Bryan — Essential Tremor, MRgFUS candidate.** A Scottish trad musician with ET published in TRACS (https://tracscotland.org/blog/essential-tremor-a-musicians-perspective-by-valerie-bryan/) documents progressive loss of capability: "I can no longer play the flute or whistle, as I can't really get them to my mouth, let alone hold them there, or play them. (I can still play the piano a bit, and sing, though – I'm lucky!)." She was awaiting Magnetic Resonance-guided Focused Ultrasound treatment. The blog explicitly enumerates DAW-relevant tremor impairments: "playing musical instruments, … using a computer… Carrying cups/mugs, bowls, plates, etc, is usually impossible." ET-related social isolation and depression are flagged as a *secondary* impairment that affects creative flow in its own right.

**NIME / ADMI longitudinal and survey studies:**

- **Netychords** (Davanzo, Avanzini, Ludovico, https://avanzini.di.unimi.it/downloads/publications/davanzo_chira23.pdf) reports a child with cerebral palsy who, working with this ADMI, "achieved a significant milestone, namely the enrollment in Portugal's Arts Education Program." One of the few longitudinal cases of *re-entry* into music-making via an adaptive interface.
- **DuoRhythmo** (CHI 2023, http://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3544548.3581285), evaluated with n=5 ALS participants, reports an average System Usability Scale (SUS) score of **79.5** and qualitative descriptors "fun, empowering, accessible, easy to use, engaging, and stimulating." SUS > 68 is conventionally "above average," but this is *eye-tracking*, not tremor.
- A gaze-driven xylophone interface (https://exa.ai/library/publication/wdb1cwxbwld) reports SUS items with mean Likert ratings in the 1.7–4.0 range on a 5-point scale (n=9).
- **DexPlay** (Berkeley AHD 2023, https://edg.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/AHD-2023-group9.pdf) is a passive wrist dampener designed after a case-study interview with an ET guitarist who had given up guitar. It targets the flexion-extension wrist axis specifically — illustrating the principle of *anatomically targeted* intervention.
- **Ayre** (QuackHacks 2026 hackathon, https://github.com/0xrpheus/ayre) explicitly includes a "Tremor smoothing" slider on a webcam-tracked hand controller; documented as an accessibility feature, not a research study.
- A classification study on kinematic and EMG signals associated with pathological tremor (MDPI Entropy 2023, https://www.mdpi.com/1099-4300/25/1/114) reports LSTM f1 = 0.98 on raw EMG; template-based assistive instruments in the same area report gesture-classifier precision as low as 0.4.
- **TRECEY: Tremor Compensation using Eye-tracking** (2025, https://exa.ai/library/publication/hbp3wtxgkbj) is another eye-tracking-based tremor compensation interface.

## Creative flow: what the literature actually says

The flow-state literature (Csikszentmihalyi's nine-dimensional construct; reproduced verbatim in https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3837225/) lists the necessary conditions for flow: challenge-skill balance, action-awareness merging, clear goals, unambiguous feedback, concentration, sense of control, loss of self-consciousness, time transformation, and autotelic experience. A Drexel Creativity Research Lab fMRI/EEG study of 32 jazz guitarists (https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/brain-scans-of-jazz-musicians-reveal-how-to-reach-a-creative-flow-state/; https://mesplaisirs.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/1-s2.0-S0028393224000393-main.pdf; https://drexel.edu/news/archive/2024/March/New-Neuroimaging-Study-Reveals-How-the-Brain-Achieves-a-Creative-Flow-State) found that higher-domain-experience performers enter flow through **release of conscious control**, not hyperfocus — once a motor program is well-learned, *letting go* of micro-corrections enables flow. **This is the central tension for any tremor-filtering system.** A system that demands the user micro-manage thresholds, or that introduces perceptible lag and forces compensation, fights directly against the action-awareness merging and sense of control necessary for flow.

Quantitative link between tremor symptoms and flow disruption is not in the published HCI literature. What is documented is the existence of **biopsychosocial cascades**: ET patients document social withdrawal, anxiety in performance contexts, and depression (https://tracscotland.org/blog/essential-tremor-a-musicians-perspective-by-valerie-bryan/) — each of which independently erodes flow prerequisite states. Samuel Smith's reported 50–150-attempt/demo workflow is a flow-destroying loop by construction, even though it solves the symptom enough to finish an album.

## Sensitivity threshold calibration: what is and isn't documented

Although no peer-reviewed study isolates threshold sensitivity for musicians with tremor, two indirect streams exist.

1. **VKM (CHI 2022)** reports quantitatively how threshold tightening trades false positives vs. false negatives as a function of training-set size and gesture-production variability (https://cs.ucf.edu/~jjl/pubs/Taranta2022.pdf). With a single training sample, the threshold must be loose to compensate; with dense data, it can be tight without losing gestures. Implication: a *per-user calibration phase* of even 20–30 demonstration gestures could allow substantially tighter thresholds than the "Aggressive / Balanced / Light" taxonomies commercial tools use.

2. **SteadyMouse's manual** documents the trade-off space empirically: at 95% filter strength "the mouse will feel like it's in molasses but should at least be smooth." Reducing by ~10–20 percentage points introduces some tremor leakage in exchange for responsiveness (https://www.steadymouse.com/manual/). This mirrors the VKM finding that variability-driven inflation of thresholds is necessary in performance contexts.

No published study reports composition completion times as a function of filter sensitivity, but anecdotally AI-mediated workflows (Smith's 50–150 attempts) and adaptive-instrument workflows (Netychords' multi-year adaptive redesign over many sessions) suggest **multiple-orders-of-magnitude overheads for naive approaches** vs. well-tuned pipelines.

The single most consistent finding across all examined sources is that **the asymmetry between latency and tremor-cancellation frequency matters more than raw filter strength** — and the only settings a current commercial or research tool exposes to a user to control it are coarse sliders (SteadyMouse) or coarse MIDI gates (Ableton's Velocity MIDI effect).

## Motor skill retention when switching between adaptive and standard interfaces

The strongest longitudinal evidence comes from outside the DAW literature but is directly applicable:

- The **Cymis** nursing-home study (https://exa.ai/library/publication/wb8qdd8w23g) tracked 31 disabled clients playing a score-programmed electronic instrument for an average of **5.6 years** (some up to 7 years). Of those 31: **13 (42%)** showed measurable upper-limb motor progress, **17 (55%)** showed no change (5 of whom initially progressed then regressed), and **1 (3%)** deteriorated. Direct evidence that adaptive musical interfaces can **support motor retention over multi-year horizons**, contrary to the assumption that assistive tools cause atrophy.
- Task-specific bowing tremor is itself evidence that motor systems retain highly specific trained programs decades into disease — the violinist in PMC4117185 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4117185/) developed a *new* task-specific tremor post-lobectomy only when *playing*, not during unrelated arm use, demonstrating that pathological and trained motor programs are dissociable at the neurological level. Consistent with the design principle that adaptive systems should target *only* the tremor-bearing signal dimension, not the learned intentional dimension.

No published study, however, directly tracks motor-skill loss or gain when a professional musician with movement disorder toggles between a tremor-filtered interface and a standard one (e.g., turning SteadyMouse off). This remains an open empirical question.

## Evidence-vs-claim table

| Claim in brief | Evidence status |
|---|---|
| Ableton Live has "MIDI velocity smoothing" | Partly true — the *Velocity* MIDI effect provides Gate/Clip/Random modes, but it is memoryless and acts on loudness, not tremor (https://www.ableton.com/en/live-manual/12/live-midi-effect-reference/) |
| Ableton Live markets this for tremor | False — forum users adopt it as a workaround (https://forum.ableton.com/viewtopic.php?t=120139); no productization |
| Logic Pro's Smart Controls include tremor compensation | False — not in any official Apple documentation (https://support.apple.com/guide/logicpro/smart-controls-overview-lgcp7e59f24b/mac; https://support.apple.com/content/dam/edam/applecare/images/en_US/otherassets/accessibility/vpat_logic_pro_2024.pdf) |
| SteadyMouse is a tremor-aware cursor tool | True, extensively documented (https://www.steadymouse.com/manual/) |
| SteadyMouse distinguishes vibrato from tremor | False — operates at the OS cursor layer; no musical semantics |
| Pathological tremor is 4–12 Hz and separable from vibrato | Partly true (tremor band overlaps 3–15 Hz), but separation must exploit *regularity and shape*, not rate alone (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4053556/; https://pubs.aip.org/asa/jasa/article/130/1/EL1/907816/Vibrato-and-tremor-extent-spectrum-Algorithm-and) |
| Gesture rejection in HCI has been characterized with false-positive rates | True — VKM/CHI 2022 is the canonical reference (https://cs.ucf.edu/~jjl/pubs/Taranta2022.pdf); false positives are documented as more harmful than false negatives |
| Composition completion times vary with tremor-filter sensitivity | **Not documented in any peer-reviewed source accessed** |
| User satisfaction scores vary with sensitivity | Indirectly: SUS scores exist for ADMIs (DuoRhythmo SUS 79.5 — n=5 ALS; xylophone interface 1.7–4.0 Likert — n=9) but not against tremor thresholds |
| Motor skill retention changes when switching adaptive ↔ standard | **Not documented in any peer-reviewed source accessed**; closest analogue is the multi-year Cymis study (https://exa.ai/library/publication/wb8qdd8w23g) |

## Synthesis

What the literature has not yet produced, and what an honest reading of the evidence suggests is missing, is a longitudinal, randomized comparison of composition completion time and flow-state metrics across (a) no-filter, (b) cursor-level filter (SteadyMouse), and (c) MIDI-semantic filter conditions for professional musicians with movement disorders. The infrastructure for such a study exists — the SUS instruments, the Flow State Scale (Martin & Jackson, 2008), and the VKM-style rejection framework — but the application to expressive musical input remains future work. The asymmetry between latency and tremor-cancellation frequency is the central design trade-off, and the only exposure points users currently have are coarse sliders (SteadyMouse) and coarse MIDI gates (Ableton Velocity Gate mode) — while the HCI literature has demonstrated that finer-grained rejection *is achievable in principle*, including preserving intentional motion through tremor, but has not crossed over into DAW-level real-time MIDI pipelines.
